$comment: Compliance banned-pattern registry (CLAUDE.md hard constraint 3, BUILD_SPEC §8). Patterns are case-insensitive JS regexes applied to every line of every text file under src/ (content, pages, components, layouts, lib, styles — see SCAN_DIRS in scripts/lint-claims.mjs). THIS LIST ONLY EVER GROWS — removing or loosening an entry requires the human operator. Keep patterns precise: a false positive costs a review; a false negative costs a compliance violation.
$allowlistComment: Operator-authorized exception (2026-07-20, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md): the client directed publication of mg-keyed GLP-1 price tiers, and the operator confirmed the override after the full compliance flag (FDA's 2026 warning-letter campaign on compounded-GLP-1 advertising was presented). These EXACT strings — and nothing else — are stripped from a line before the banned categories are applied; the categories themselves are untouched, and a quantity that merely contains one of these strings (e.g. a longer number) still fails. Adding, changing, or removing a string requires the human operator. Reformatted later the same day at the client's direction ('@' → 'vial:'); same five tiers, same prices — a like-for-like swap, not an expansion. Second authorization (2026-07-21, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md): the two per-unit neuromodulator price strings, published verbatim from the client's product sheet after the constraint-3 flag. The dosing category gained per-unit patterns in the same change, so unit-keyed language stays banned everywhere outside these exact strings. Narrowed and reformatted 2026-07-30 at the client's direction (recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md): the flat-dollar halves came off and '/ unit' became 'per unit' — '$10 per unit' and '$12 per unit' replace the two originals; same per-unit figures, a reduction rather than an expansion, with the registry and the page's priceLines changed together in one commit. Third authorization (2026-07-21, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md): the Evolus ranking sentence — the first non-price, superiority-class entry — published on the operator's confirmation that the designation comes from Evolus (also live on the practice's own site); the operator declined the attributed wording after the flag. '#1'/'number one'/'best' remain banned everywhere outside this exact string; the self-test's exactness proof generalized from dosing-only to any-category in the same change (a superiority-class string's near-miss variant trips superiority, not dosing). Fourth authorization (2026-07-22, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md): Biote's FDA disclaimer sentence, resolving {{BIOTE_FDA_DISCLAIMER}}. This entry is different in kind from the first three — it does not permit copy the client wants to publish, it permits text a regulator effectively requires, and without it the mandatory §7.8 disclosure could not render at all (it had been shipping as a visible placeholder token). The sentence names the four verbs the disease-claims category bans, which is exactly why that category catches it; those verbs remain banned everywhere outside this exact string, and the self-test's exactness proof covers it like any other entry. Because stripping is per line, the sentence must live on ONE source line wherever it appears — see src/components/BioteDisclaimer.astro. Fifth authorization (2026-08-04, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md): four curriculum-topic strings for the /injector-training page (Private Injector Training, the site's professional-audience offering), published flyer-verbatim at the client's direction after the compliance flag — the operator declined the recommended paraphrase. They are course-topic titles containing no quantities. Unlike every prior entry they are enumerated in exact <li>-wrapped source form, for a mechanical reason: the first string's banned word is string-initial, and the self-test's digit-prefix near-miss proof needs a word boundary for the category to re-trip — the '>' supplies it. The wrap also binds the exception to the exact attribute-less list-item source line, tighter than bare text. Stripping is per line AND case-sensitive, so each string must appear exactly as enumerated, on one source line, in registry case; this vocabulary stays banned everywhere outside these four exact strings, which render on the training page only.
allowedStrings: These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. These products are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

categories.name: dosing
categories.description: Doses, units, quantities, reconstitution, frequency/protocols, titration — banned in any form, anywhere (BUILD_SPEC §8.1).

categories.name: disease-claims
categories.description: Treat/cure/prevent/diagnose language and disease names in any context (BUILD_SPEC §8.2, §7.7 glutathione rule). 'treats' is banned; 'treatment' as a noun is fine.

categories.name: superiority
categories.description: Unsubstantiated superiority claims (BUILD_SPEC §8.4). {{EVOLUS_CLAIM}} resolved 2026-07-21: the exact Evolus ranking sentence in allowedStrings is the ONLY permitted '#1' usage.

categories.description: Per-line banned angles from BUILD_SPEC §7: GLP-1 weight/blood-sugar/appetite promises, peptide recovery/anti-aging claims, immunity-benefit extensions, investigational-as-approved framing.
